title: Ops Heuristic Lab — Weekly Debrief
content:
Purpose:
This is the Ops Heuristic Lab weekly debrief — pragmatic notes for the on-call handoffs, a short incident digest, SLO signal highlights, and the running action list. This doc is intentionally lightweight: aim is a quick read for the incoming shift and to capture experimental heuristics results from last week.

High-level summary (one line):
- Platform availability nominal; two incidents this week (one user-visible latency spike, one degraded autoscale path) — both mitigated, root cause triangulation in progress.

Incident digest (chronological):
1) Incident ID: INC-2029-1202-latency
   - Window: 2029-12-02 03:14–03:48 UTC
   - Symptom: 95th percentile token latency for hosted-api /v1/generate increased from 210ms -> 840ms for ~34 minutes. Error rate stayed <0.05%.
   - Immediate mitigation: Rolled traffic from cpu-backed fallback to lower-latency small-quantized model; temporary uplift of batch size threshold to reduce starvation.
   - Probable cause: KV-cache eviction storm triggered by an unusual prefix-distribution spike from a partner integration (large batch of long-sequence prompts). KV storage GC paused serving threads under high mem churn on one autoscale shard.
   - Current status: Postmortem draft started (linked), working hypothesis requires heap profile + kernel scheduling logs. Follow-ups assigned to Miguel (heap profile) and Jonah (autoscaler telem).

2) Incident ID: INC-2029-1205-autoscale-degrade
   - Window: 2029-12-05 18:05–18:22 UTC
   - Symptom: Dedicated cluster failed to spin one hot-pool node within target SLA (60s), causing transient routing to lower-cost zone and 5xx spike for <10m for a small set of tenant routes.
   - Root cause: Race in the preflight health-check: liveness probe returned READY before NVLink peer attach had completed; health-check considered node available and sent traffic prematurely.
   - Remediation: Tightened preflight health-check to verify GPU driver status + NVLink attach flag. Backport PR merged to release branch (link in linked_artifacts).
   - Current status: Complete (monitoring for recurrence).

SLO / signal snapshot (as of 2029-12-07 06:00 UTC):
- Hosted API latency SLO (p50/p95/p99): 120ms / 320ms / 640ms. Weekly p95 now at 280ms (within buffer), but p99 shows tail due to INC-1202.
- Uptime SLO: 99.95% monthly — no breaches in rolling 30d.
- Error budget remaining (monthly): 78%
- Alert churn: +12% vs prior week (mostly noise from autoscaler flaps and a mis-tuned synthetic check).

Heuristic Lab experiments + observations:
- Batch-Adaptive Throttling (prototype): Enabled on one low-traffic cluster. Observed 8% per-token cost reduction for conversational workloads but a small increase in 95th percentile latency during cold-starts. Hypothesis: threshold tuning required. Action: Hannah to run A/B with adjusted cold-start grace window.
- KV-cache GC tuning: Enabled conservative GC windows on two nodes; reduced eviction storms but slightly increased memory footprint. Need to scale node pool or improve eviction heuristics.
- Synthetic probe instability: Synthetic checks for quantized-models producing occasional OOM on tiny containers; raises false positives in uptime alerting. Created a short-term filter to ignore OOMs with baked-in retry count >2.

Runbook / handoff-critical checks (incoming shift checklist):
- Verify primary SLO dashboard for p95 and p99 latency; check the "tail spikes" panel.
- Confirm autoscaler health: check 'hot-pool-ready' metric and recent scale events (>0 events in last 15m triggers review).
- Run KV-cache eviction dashboard: any node with eviction_rate > 10/s -> escalate to infra oncall.
- Confirm newest preflight health-check version on production branch (tag: v2029.11.3-pf).
- Validate that the 'Batch-Adaptive' experiment flag is set to false for tenant-critical flows (we only want it in experiment clusters).
- Pager escalation contacts: primary oncall -> Miguel Torres; secondary -> Priya Anand; infra escalation -> Jonah Patel.

Open action items (owner, ETA):
- Miguel: produce heap + GC flame graphs for INC-1202 (ETA 2029-12-09).
- Jonah: add NVLink attach metric to node preflight probe and add an observability alert if attach_time > 30s (ETA 2029-12-08).
- Hannah: run A/B for Batch-Adaptive cold-start grace window and report cost/latency delta (ETA 2029-12-14).
- Priya: audit synthetic probe filtering rules and push filter hotfix for quantized-model OOM false positives (ETA 2029-12-08).

Notes for on-call and playbook adjustments:
- Add a short checklist item to run a quick KV-cache smoke-check after large customer data migrations. Several customers have hit unusual prefix shapes after migration.
- Consider introducing per-tenant cold-start grace policy to reduce p95 noise for predictable long-sequence customers.
- Autoscaler preflight: add backstop that prevents routing to a node until NVLink attach metric present for at least 5 consecutive seconds.

Communication + customer impact:
- INC-1202: Outreach to impacted partner sent on 2029-12-03; they acknowledged and provided example payloads. Tentative follow-up sync scheduled 2029-12-10.
- No customer credits expected at this time.

Misc capture / notes to self:
- Found a weird correlation between synthetic quantized OOMs and nightly image builds; further investigation may point to a packaging change.
- Small win: instrumentation added to the autoscale agent reduced noise for that alert by 22% — keep rolling out.

Appendix / links (quick):
- Postmortem draft (INC-1202): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-1202-draft
- Autoscale preflight PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1920
- Batch-Adaptive experiment dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/exp/batch-adaptive

End of brief. Incoming oncall: thanks — scan the checklist, pick up the open action items assigned to you, and leave notes in this doc (append new section with your name/date).

-- Priya
